C.D.S.I. Fan Lien Pih was never appointed by the
Special Branch or any other section of the Municipal Police
to act as mediator in settling the strike in the Shanghai
Electric Construction Co. He did not produce any letter to
this effect either at the offices of the Company or elsewhere
and as a matter of fact was never in possession of such a
letter.

The members of the staff of the Intelligence Section
of the Special Branch have in accordance with your instructions
been warned to discourage publicity calculated to give the
impression that the Police have acted as mediators in settling
strikes.

May 16, 1930. Morning translation.

LABOUR

THE STRIKE OF TRAMWAY EMPLOYEES

The China Times and other
local newspapers publish the following report:-
The drivers and conductors of
the Shanghai Tramway Company have been on strike
for 22 days. Yesterday afternoon the Strike
Committee appointed representatives to negotiate
with the management. The Special Branch of the
S.M.P. appointed C.D.S.I. Pan Lien Pih to act as
mediator. The management, however, remained
firm in its attitude and strongly rejected all the
demands submitted by the strikers. The negotiations
had no result.

The strikers will hold a
general meeting at 8 a.m. May 16 to discuss ways and
means to deal with the situation.
According to another report,
about 600 tramway employees assembled in the An Tung
Lodging House at 10 a.m. yesterday awaiting the
representatives of the Tramway Company to open
negotiations as had been previously arranged. However,
the representatives of the Company did not attend
and at 2 p.m. C.D.S.I. Pan Lien Pih and his interpreter
arrived and requested the strikers to appoint
representatives to go with him to the Tramway Company
at No. 7 Soochow Road to open negotiations.
C.D.S.I. Pan Lien Pih and the
representatives of the strikers arrived at the
Tramway Company at 2.05 p.m. and were received by the
General Manager and three others. The labour
representatives then submitted the following minimum
demands which had been fixed by the Strike Committee:-
(1) An increase of $3. each per month as well as a rice
allowance of $3. each per month.
(2) Double pay for Sundays and during greyhound races.
(3) Usual pay for the period of the strike.
(4) The release of the arrested workers and their
reinstatement.
(5) Reinstatement of unemployed men.
C.D.S.I. Pan Lien Pih here produced a letter proving
that he had been appointed by the Special Branch of the
S.M.P. to act as a mediator.
The management accepted the 1st
demand but mechanics will be given an increase of 90
cents per month because they had been given an increase
of 7 cents per day during January which will bring their
total amount of increase to $3. per month. All the
other demands were rejected especially the 5th demand
calling for the reinstatement of unemployed men.
Despite the repeated requests of the labour representatives
the management could not be persuaded to re-consider
its decision. The labour representatives left
the Company at 5 p.m.
When leaving, the labour representatives,
in reply to a question of the General Manager, stated that
the question of resuming work would be decided by a
general meeting of strikers to be held on May 16.

1930年5月16日。晨间译文。

劳工

电车职员罢工

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸刊登了以下报道：
上海电车公司的司机和售票员已罢工22天。昨日下午，罢工委员会指派代表与管理层进行谈判。上海公共租界工部局警务处特别处指派华人侦探副督察 Pan Lien Pih 担任调解人。然而，管理层态度强硬，强烈拒绝了罢工者提出的所有要求。谈判没有结果。

罢工者将于5月16日上午8时举行全体会议，讨论应对局势的方法。
据另一则报道，约600名电车职员于昨日上午10时在安东旅社集合，等待电车公司代表按先前安排开启谈判。然而，公司代表未出席，下午2时，华人侦探副督察 Pan Lien Pih 及其翻译到达，并要求罢工者指派代表随他前往苏州路7号的电车公司开启谈判。
华人侦探副督察 Pan Lien Pih 和罢工者代表于下午2时05分抵达电车公司，受到总经理及其他三人的接待。劳工代表随后提交了由罢工委员会确定的以下最低要求：
(1) 每人每月加薪3元，以及每人每月3元的米贴。
(2) 星期日及赛狗日期间双倍工资。
(3) 罢工期间照常发薪。
(4) 释放被捕工人并恢复其职务。
(5) 复职失业人员。
华人侦探副督察 Pan Lien Pih 此时出示了一封信，证明他已被上海公共租界工部局警务处特别处任命为调解人。
管理层接受了第1项要求，但技工每月仅加薪90角，因为他们在1月份每天已加薪7分，这将使他们的总加薪额达到每月3元。所有其他要求均被拒绝，特别是要求复职失业人员的第5项要求。
尽管劳工代表反复请求，管理层仍不肯重新考虑其决定。劳工代表于下午5时离开公司。
离开时，劳工代表回答总经理的提问时表示，是否复工的问题将由5月16日举行的罢工者全体会议决定。

C. I. D. REGISTER
No. I. O. D. 1207.
Date 19...5...30.

Extract from Intelligence Report 6.5.30.

The strike of the employees of the Shanghai Tramway Co.
continues.

Some twenty representatives of strikers in various departments
held a meeting between 5 and 6.15 p.m. May 5, in a room in the
Grand Hotel, Pakhoi and Thibet Roads corner, at which the
following resolutions were discussed and passed:-

1. That all points of dispute effecting employees be settled
before resumption of work takes place.

2. That a general meeting of strikers be held on the morning of
May 8 (venue not decided upon).

3. That motorman 195 being a labour traitor be assaulted and
that Conductor 291 be warned by a letter against his conduct
towards the strikers.

4. That strict measures against the Russian drivers of the buses
be devised.

5. That the manager of the Company give written assurance that
no representatives of the strikers be dismissed when work
is resumed.

6. That no individual strikers be permitted to conduct
negotiation with the Company.

7. That the dismissal of an employee named Siao Wong of the
Publicity Supt.'s Staff, be demanded for his inimical
attitude against the employees.

C.P.

摘自1930年5月6日的情报报告。

上海电车公司职员的罢工仍在继续。

来自各部门的约二十名罢工者代表于5月5日下午5时至6时15分在北海路与西藏路转角的大饭店的一个房间内举行会议，讨论并通过了以下决议：

1. 在复工之前，解决影响职员的所有争议点。

2. 于5月8日上午举行罢工者全体会议（地点未定）。

3. 殴打身为工贼的195号司机，并以信函警告291号售票员，因其对罢工者的行为不当。

4. 制定针对公交车俄罗斯司机的严厉措施。

5. 公司经理须书面保证，复工后不会解雇任何罢工者代表。

6. 不允许个别罢工者与公司进行谈判。

7. 要求解雇宣传主管职员中的一名名为 Siao Wong 的雇员，因其对职员持敌对态度。

(C.I.D.) Office Notes

Tramway Strike

A strikers' delegation composed of one mechanic, one motorman and one conductor called on the General Manager this forenoon and presented attached demands.

In view of the fact that the mechanic and motorman were men having very indifferent records, the manager was loathe to treat with them and intimated that he would be only too pleased to discuss the situation with a delegation which really represented the workers, but in this particular instance he was inclined towards the belief that his visitors did not represent the entire body of workers. The conductor, who although of little service has quite a good record, suggested that the Manager supply a list of names of workers from amongst whom they could select delegates. Names of eighteen of the best conductors were supplied following which the delegation withdrew to consult with their colleagues.

As can be seen, the demands are more or less the same as were contained in an inflammatory handbill which was sent through the post to the Traffic Superintendent two days before the strike.

Huo Robertson

（刑事侦缉处）办公室笔记

电车罢工

一个由一名技工、一名司机和一名售票员组成的罢工者代表团于今天上午拜访了总经理，并提交了所附的要求。

鉴于该技工和司机的记录非常糟糕，经理不愿与他们打交道，并表示他很乐意与真正代表工人的代表团讨论局势，但在这种情况下，他倾向于认为来访者并不代表全体工人。那位售票员虽然服务年限不长，但记录相当好，建议经理提供一份工人名单，以便他们从中挑选代表。随后提供了十八名最佳售票员的名单，代表团随即退下与其同事商议。

可以看出，这些要求与罢工前两天通过邮寄发送给交通主管的一份煽动性传单中的内容大致相同。

Translation.
Shanghai, 28th April, 1930.

The General Manager,
Shanghai Tramway Co.,

Dear Sir,
We have the honour to inform you that as the price of rice has risen from $12 to $21.40 per picul, we are unable to maintain our daily livelihood. The French Tramway Co. and Municipal Council have increased in succession the wages and rice allowance of their workers except our magnificent Shanghai Tramway Co. which disregards the distress of the workers. Therefore on the 22nd instant, we decided to submit increases of wages and rice allowance and betterment of treatment to the company and you through our club. The next day, your Company only announced a rice allowance of three and seven cents respectively without mentioning the rest of our demands. As the Company has not replied us within a limited time, we are of the opinion that the Company has no sincerity to accept our demands. Consequently, we are obliged to stage a strike. We beg now to dispatch three representatives to your company to submit our following demands and hope you will give us a satisfactory reply:
(1) A flat increase of eight dollars each man and each month.
(2) A rice allowance of three dollars each man and each month.
(3) To recognise the club as having the power to represent the entire workers. The company to subsidise an office expense of three hundred dollars a month.

上海，1930年4月28日。

总经理，
上海电车公司，

尊敬的先生：
我们荣幸地通知您，由于米价从每担12元涨至21.40元，我们无法维持日常生计。法国电车公司和工部局相继增加了工人的工资和米贴，唯独我们伟大的上海电车公司无视工人的困境。因此，我们在本月22日决定通过我们的俱乐部向公司和您提交增加工资、米贴及改善待遇的要求。次日，贵公司仅宣布分别发放三分和七分的米贴，而未提及我们的其余要求。由于公司未在规定期限内回复我们，我们认为公司没有诚意接受我们的要求。因此，我们被迫举行罢工。我们现在恳请派遣三名代表向贵公司提交以下要求，并希望您给予我们满意的答复：
(1) 每人每月固定加薪八元。
(2) 每人每月三元米贴。
(3) 承认俱乐部有权代表全体工人。公司每月补贴三百元办公费用。

those who work. Two additional days for twenty days' work each
month and four additional days for twenty five days' work each

(6) Full pay during the strike.
(7) Workers not to be dismissed without cause.
(8) Release of arrested workers. No worker to be arrested
in future.

(11) Mechanics to be provided with French passes.
(12) Any conductor who takes out a ticket box or motorman
who takes out his driving handles to receive one day's pay. Double
pay for those whose work is prolonged during greyhound races.
(13) One month's retiring gratuity each year to be given
to each worker when he resigns or when he is discharged.

Subject (in full) Meeting of the Employees of the Shanghai Tramway Company.
Made by D.S. O'Rourke Forwarded by [签名]
Sir,
About 50 employees of the Shanghai Tramway Co., held a
meeting at No.1066 Whashing Road at about 10.30 am 27-4-30.
The following resolutions were discussed and passed:-
Demands
1. All men in the employ of the Tramway Co. to receive
$8.00 per month rise of pay.
2. All men to receive $5.00 extra for rice money during
the high cost of living.
3. The Shanghai Tramway Co. to pay $300.00 per month
for the upkeep of the Chinese Tramway Union.
4. All men to receive double pay for working on Sundays
and Holidays.
5. Every man while on the sick list is to receive full
pay.
6. During the present strike, all employees are to be
paid their wages as usual.
7. All workers arrested by the Police must be released.
8. No worker must be dismissed without the sanction of the
Union. No Russians are to be employed in the place of
dismissed workers.
9. All Kiosks to have warm tea for the convenience of the
drivers and conductors.
10. Raincoats must be supplied for boys on point duty.
11. All employees to be exempt from paying fares on other
tramways.
12. All men on Luna Park duty must receive double pay.

要求

Strike Regulations for Workers
1. All workers must obey the orders issued by the Tramway Union.
2. All workers must remain on strike and not resume work until
all demands are met.
3. If a worker breaks any of the regulations issued by the
Tramway Union, he will be assaulted by the other workers.
3a. If any worker attempts to resume work before the strike
is settled, he will be assaulted by the other workers.
3b. If any worker spreads rumours about resuming work, he will
be assaulted by the other workers.
To-morrow morning, 28-4-30, another meeting will be held
and every man is to attend in uniform without cap.

Extract from Intelligence Report D.R.446

It is reported that some thirty motormen and conductors of
the Shanghai Tramways and several representatives of the workers
of the Omnibus Company, French Tramway Co. and the Shanghai Power
Co. held a meeting on a piece of vacant ground off Glen Road on
the night of April 24 at which they decided to bring about a strike
of Tramway Employees to show sympathy with the Bus Company workers.
Some 700 motormen, conductors, etc. of the Shanghai Tramways
attached to the Wayside Shed (Route 6, 7, 8 and 9) and to Baikal
Road Depot (Railless Routes 17 and 18) went on strike at 6 a.m.
to-day to show sympathy with the Bus Company workers. The
mechanics in Baikal Road Depot and all employes at Hart Road Depot
are working as usual. Services are being maintained from Hart
Road Depot.
It is reported that the strikers propose presenting the
following demands to the Company:-
1. A rice bonus of $3 per man per month.
2. An increase of $8 per month in wages and an annual increase
of $5 per month each successive year.
3. Observance of Sundays and festivals as holidays with pay or
double wages for employees compelled to perform duty on
these days.
4. A supply of tea at each clock kiosk.

I. O. D. 1207

情报报告 D.R.446 摘录

据报，约三十名上海电车公司的司机和售票员，以及公共汽车公司、法商电车公司和上海电力公司工人的几名代表，于4月24日晚在格伦路（Glen Road）旁的一块空地上举行会议，决定发动电车雇员罢工，以表示对公共汽车公司工人的同情。
隶属于路边车棚（6、7、8和9路）和贝加尔路车场（无轨电车17和18路）的约700名上海电车公司司机、售票员等，于今晨6时开始罢工，以表示对公共汽车公司工人的同情。贝加尔路车场的机械工和哈特路车场的所有雇员照常工作。哈特路车场维持着服务。
据报，罢工者拟向公司提出以下要求：-
1. 每人每月3元的米贴奖金。
2. 每月工资增加8元，此后每年每月再递增5元。
3. 星期日和节假日作为带薪休假，或迫使员工在这些日子执勤者发给双薪。
4. 每个时钟岗亭须供应茶水。

page_data.en:
Extract from Intelligence Report
D.R. 447.

The strike of some 700 motor-men and conductors of the
Wayside Depot of the Shanghai Tramway Company which commenced
at 6 a.m. April 25 extended to the mechanics in Baikal Road
Sheds about 11 a.m. and to Hart Road Depot about 1p.m. when
the trams were withdrawn from the streets. The strike
continues to-day. About 1,400 conductors and drivers and
500 mechanics are affected.
At 12.45 p.m. April 25 one Tsang Yen Zung, a tram
conductor, was arrested at Sinza and Carter Roads Corner by
the Municipal Police for intimidating the employees of the
Company to go on strike.

情报报告摘录
D.R. 447。

上海电车公司路边车场约700名司机和售票员于4月25日上午6时开始的罢工，于上午11时左右蔓延至贝加尔路车棚的机械工，并于下午1时左右蔓延至哈特路车场，届时电车从街道上撤回。罢工今日仍在继续。受影响者约有1,400名售票员和司机，以及500名机械工。
1930年4月25日下午12时45分，一名名为曾延宗（Tsang Yen Zung，音译）的电车售票员，因恐吓公司雇员参加罢工，在新闸路与卡特路（Carter Road，音译）转角处被工部局警察逮捕。
